text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Leaders of Nigeria's five registered political parties to tour some European countries in March to canvass support for the military government's transition programme.
- Government appoints monitoring officers who will ensure banks, individuals, insurance and finance houses comply with all sections of the Foreign Exchange Decree.
- Securitymen drafted to the premises of Lagos-based Atlantic Textile Mills to maintain peace and order following a dispute between management and staff over working conditions.

- The Bini people in midwestern Edo state want to seek an International Court of Justice order to compel the British government return over 5,000 bronze and ivory treasures taken during the invasion of their kingdom by Britain in 1897.

- Families of those aboard a presidential jet which crashed last January in northern Nigeria, killing the eldest son of military ruler General Sani Abacha and 13 others, are yet to be compensated, Thisday checks reveal.
